links.outcome: LLM accuracy and prediction flips under misinformation framing and layperson rewriting perturbations
links.effect: MF degrades accuracy by 7.2 pp on average with prediction flip rates of 9-38 percent, even when claims are labelled unsupported; LR causes only 1.4 pp degradation.
links.quote: Experiments show that MF degrades accuracy by 7.2 pp on average with prediction flip rates of 9-38 percent, even when claims are explicitly labelled as unsupported; LR causes only 1.4 pp degradation.

links.outcome: Consistency of LLM answers when patients rephrase symptoms in everyday language
links.effect: Layperson rewriting caused only 1.4 pp accuracy degradation, while misinformation framing caused 7.2 pp degradation on average.
links.quote: Experiments show that MF degrades accuracy by 7.2 pp on average with prediction flip rates of 9-38 percent, even when claims are explicitly labelled as unsupported; LR causes only 1.4 pp degradation.

screen.reason: The study develops an automated benchmark to test LLM robustness to prompt perturbations (misinformation framing and layperson rewriting) in public health contexts, but does not test an organizational deployment guardrail or safeguard intervention.
